qt: to the Commission Cristina Maestre (S&D) Subject:

The United Kingdom plans to suspend tariffs on certain agri-food products from third countries, including fresh and chilled garlic, from 26 November 2026 until the end of 2028. As a result of this decision, EU producers, especially those from Spain, are concerned about the risk of their exports being crowded out by those of competitors with lower production costs. Other sectors, such as the fruit and vegetable sector, could also be impacted. Without calling into question the UK’s trade autonomy, action needs to be taken to preserve balanced trade relations and protect the competitiveness of our producers. In view of the above: 1.
Does the Commission intend to make urgent diplomatic representations to the UK authorities to push for garlic to be excluded from the tariff suspensions?

Will it assess the impact of the suspensions on other EU agri-food products and promote support measures, market diversification or the reconsideration of the UK measures when they cause significant harm?

What guarantees does it intend to promote in order to preserve traceability and prevent trade diversion or tariff circumvention, especially in light of the negotiations on a future sanitary and phytosanitary agreement between the European Union and the United Kingdom?
